answer: Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 34% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Because the ledge ordering is published with the umber batch, the sonnet audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. A 391 account operation therefore ties up 2 million dollars of idle capital. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
